characters.description: The son of a Brahmin in ancient India, a gifted and admired young man who nonetheless feels a deep restlessness and dissatisfaction with the teachings and rituals he has been raised in. Handsome, thoughtful, and proud, he is loved by all around him yet convinced that the wisdom handed down to him cannot bring the inner peace he seeks. Determined to find truth through his own experience rather than borrowed doctrine, he sets out on a lifelong search that will lead him through asceticism, indulgence, and every extreme of human life.
characters.name: Siddhartha

characters.description: Siddhartha's closest friend since childhood, who admires and loves him and follows him out of their village to seek enlightenment. Devoted and earnest, Govinda is more inclined than Siddhartha to trust teachers and to seek truth through established doctrine and discipline. His path repeatedly diverges from Siddhartha's, as he places his faith in following a master while his friend insists on finding wisdom alone.
characters.name: Govinda

characters.description: A respected Brahmin who has raised Siddhartha in the learning and rituals of their tradition and hopes his son will become a great scholar and priest. When Siddhartha announces he means to leave and join the wandering ascetics, his father resists, but he finally relents after Siddhartha stands unmoving in silent determination through the night.
characters.name: Siddhartha's father

characters.description: The revered enlightened teacher, known as the Buddha, whose fame draws seekers from across the land. Serene, luminous, and utterly at peace, he preaches a doctrine of the causes of suffering and the path to its end. Siddhartha recognizes his greatness and the perfection of his calm, yet declines to become his follower, reasoning that enlightenment is a matter of personal experience that cannot be passed on through any teaching, however true. Govinda, by contrast, joins the Buddha's order.
characters.name: Gotama the Buddha

characters.description: A beautiful and accomplished courtesan in the town Siddhartha reaches after leaving the ascetic life, renowned for her grace and self-possession. She agrees to teach Siddhartha the art of love in exchange for his winning wealth and fine things, and she becomes his guide into the world of the senses and material life. Worldly, clever, and independent, she is drawn to Siddhartha's strange inner stillness even as she leads him deeper into pleasure and desire.
characters.name: Kamala

characters.description: A wealthy merchant to whom Kamala directs Siddhartha so he can earn the riches he needs. Anxious, acquisitive, and governed by gain and worry, Kamaswami takes Siddhartha on as an assistant and is baffled by his employee's detachment from success and failure alike. Under him Siddhartha learns trade and grows prosperous, though he treats business almost as a game, a contrast that highlights the merchant's fretful bondage to money.
characters.name: Kamaswami

characters.description: A humble ferryman who carries travelers across a great river. Calm, kind, and remarkably attentive, he speaks little but listens deeply and has found a quiet wisdom by living beside the water and learning from it. When Siddhartha first crosses the river he senses something rare in the man, and Vasudeva later becomes his companion and gentle guide, teaching him to hear what the river has to say.
characters.name: Vasudeva

characters.description: The child of Siddhartha and Kamala, a boy raised in the comfort and refinement of the town and unaware of his father until circumstance brings them together late in the story. Spoiled, willful, and grieving, he resents the simple, poor life of the ferry and the quiet man who tries to love him, and he longs to return to the world he knew, straining against every attempt to hold him.
characters.name: Siddhartha's son
